pairs: Profectus ergo Jacob venit in terram orientalem.
And so Jacob, setting out, arrived in the eastern land.
And he saw a well in a field,
tres quoque greges ovium accubantes juxta eum:
and also three flocks of sheep reclining near it.
For the animals were watered from it,
et os ejus grandi lapide claudebatur.
and its mouth was closed with a great stone.
Morisque erat ut cunctis ovibus congregatis devolverent lapidem,
And the custom was, when all the sheep were gathered together, to roll away the stone.
et refectis gregibus rursum super os putei ponerent.
And when the flocks had been refreshed, they placed it over the mouth of the well again.
And he said to the shepherds,
et ecce Rachel filia ejus venit cum grege suo.
“And behold, his daughter Rachel approaches with his flock.”
nec est tempus ut reducantur ad caulas greges:
and it is not time to return the flocks to the sheepfold.
Give the sheep to drink first,
et sic eas ad pastum reducite.
and then lead them back to pasture.”
until all the animals are gathered together
et amoveamus lapidem de ore putei,
and we remove the stone from the mouth of the well,
so that we may water the flocks.”
et ecce Rachel veniebat cum ovibus patris sui:
and behold, Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep;
and he realized that she was his maternal first cousin,
and that these were the sheep of his uncle Laban,
he removed the stone which closed the well.
Et adaquato grege, osculatus est eam:
And having watered the flock, he kissed her.
And lifting up his voice, he wept.
et indicavit ei quod frater esset patris sui,
And he revealed to her that he was a brother of her father,
at illa festinans nuntiavit patri suo.
And so, hurrying, she announced it to her father.
Qui cum audisset venisse Jacob filium sororis suæ,
And when he had heard that Jacob, his sister’s son, had arrived,
he brought him into his house.
But when he had heard the reasons for his journey,
Et postquam impleti sunt dies mensis unius,
And after the days of one month were completed,
will you serve me for nothing?
Tell me what wages you would accept.”
In truth, he had two daughters:
the name of the elder was Leah;
and truly the younger was called Rachel.
Serviam tibi pro Rachel filia tua minore, septem annis.
“I will serve you for seven years, for your younger daughter Rachel.”
Melius est ut tibi eam dem quam alteri viro:
“It is better that I give her to you than to another man;
Servivit ergo Jacob pro Rachel septem annis:
Therefore, Jacob served for seven years for Rachel.
et videbantur illi pauci dies præ amoris magnitudine.
And these seemed like only a few days, because of the greatness of love.
For now the time has been fulfilled,
so that I may go in to her.”
Qui vocatis multis amicorum turbis ad convivium,
And he, having called a great crowd of his friends to the feast,
Et vespere Liam filiam suam introduxit ad eum,
And at night, he brought in his daughter Leah to him,
giving his daughter a handmaid named Zilpah.
Ad quam cum ex more Jacob fuisset ingressus,
After Jacob had gone in to her, according to custom,
when morning had arrived, he saw Leah.
And he said to his father-in-law,
“What is it that you intended to do?
Did I not serve you for Rachel?
Non est in loco nostro consuetudinis, ut minores ante tradamus ad nuptias.
“It is not the practice in this place to give the younger in marriage first.
Complete a week of days with this mating.
et hanc quoque dabo tibi pro opere quo serviturus es mihi septem annis aliis.
And then I will give this one to you also, for the service that you will provide to me for another seven years.”
And after the week had passed,
he took Rachel as a wife.
To her, the father had given Bilhah as her servant.
And, having at last obtained the marriage he desired,
he preferred the love of the latter before the former,
serviens apud eum septem annis aliis.
and he served with him another seven years.
Videns autem Dominus quod despiceret Liam,
But the Lord, seeing that he despised Leah,
aperuit vulvam ejus, sorore sterili permanente.
opened her womb, but her sister remained barren.
Having conceived, she gave birth to a son,
and she called his name Reuben,
now my husband will love me.”
And again she conceived and bore a son,
Quoniam audivit me Dominus haberi contemptui,
“Because the Lord heard that I was treated with contempt,
he has also given this one to me.”
And she called his name Simeon.
And she conceived a third time,
and she gave birth to another son,
Nunc quoque copulabitur mihi maritus meus:
“Now likewise my husband will unite with me,
eo quod pepererim ei tres filios:
because I have borne him three sons.”
et idcirco appellavit nomen ejus Levi.
And because of this, she called his name Levi.
A fourth time she conceived and bore a son,
“Only now will I confess to the Lord.”
et ob hoc vocavit eum Judam:
